findings.highlight: Saber approaches, as if those arrows aren't even worth dodging
findings.evidenceJa: そのような物、防ぐまでもないとセイバーに迫る巨人
findings.governingReading: そのような物、防ぐまでもないとセイバーに迫る巨人 has the giant approaching Saber because he thinks the projectile is not worth blocking.
findings.explanation: The English makes Saber approach as though the arrows are not worth dodging, when the Japanese says Berserker continues pursuing her.

findings.highlight: It was a sword, I think
findings.evidenceJa: たとえそれが剣であったとしても
findings.governingReading: たとえそれが剣であったとしても is hypothetical: even if this object were a sword, it was used as an arrow and therefore functioned as one.
findings.explanation: A hypothetical concession about the sword-shaped object becomes Shirou’s belief that it was a sword.

findings.evidenceJa: バーサーカーによって叩き折られた矢
findings.governingReading: 矢 and それ refer to the singular, strange projectile that has just rolled over; the following lines track that broken object fading away.
findings.explanation: The single broken arrow is changed into multiple arrows that Berserker smashes aside.

findings.highlight: like candle wax melting in flames
findings.evidenceJa: 熱に溶ける飴のようでもある
findings.governingReading: 飴 is candy; the image is of the object thinning and disappearing like candy melting in heat.
findings.explanation: The arrow fades like melted candy in the source, but the English compares it to candle wax.
